\label{long269:thm:clock-relations}
Under the preceding hypotheses on the linear flow, choose integers $b_i\ge2$, put
$Q_n=\prod_{k\le n}b_{w_k}$ and
\[
 S_i=\sum_{n:\,w_n=i}\frac1{Q_n}\qquad(1\le i\le d).
\]
For every $c_i\in\Q$,
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^dc_iS_i\in\Q
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 c_i=\lambda(b_i-1)\quad\hbox{for all $i$ and some $\lambda\in\Q$}.
\]
The rational value is $\lambda$.  Equivalently, all rational relations
$a_0+\sum_i a_iS_i=0$ are multiples of
$(-1,b_1-1,\ldots,b_d-1)$.  Thus the span of
$1,S_1,\ldots,S_d$ has dimension $d$; each $S_i$ and each nonempty
proper unweighted sub-sum is irrational.  The full unweighted sum is
irrational exactly when the radices are not all equal.
